answer: An agent economy resists Sybils with a refundable stake bonded to slowly earned reputation. A new identity starts on a narrow ledge: tiny transaction limits and no credit, so a flood of fresh fakes buys nothing. To cross the bridge to full limits it must collect attestations from established peers who stake their own standing on its work, a whisper network where a bad attestation costs the voucher too. Faking one identity is cheap; faking hundreds that all earn real attestations costs stake, time and coordination, while one caught fake burns its bond.
